A.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are true. Gradient magnitude is largest at $t_2$ and drag equals weight at both terminal velocities at $t_1$ and $t_3$.

B.explanation: Statement 3 is false. Drag is much larger just after the parachute opens at $t_2$ than at the first terminal velocity at $t_1$.

C.explanation: Statement 1 is also true because the velocity-time gradient is steepest at $t_2$, so 2 alone is incomplete.

D.explanation: Statement 3 is false and statement 1 is true, so drag is not maximum at $t_1$ and acceleration is maximum at $t_2$.

hints: Notice where $t_1$, $t_2$ and $t_3$ sit on the velocity-time graph: $t_1$ is on the first flat high-velocity part, $t_2$ is where the curve starts to fall steeply, $t_3$ is on the second flat low-velocity part.
Recall that gradient of a velocity-time graph gives acceleration, so compare the steepness of the curve at $t_1$, $t_2$ and $t_3$ to judge statement 1.

Recall that at constant terminal velocity resultant force is zero so drag equals weight, and that opening the parachute greatly increases drag at almost the same high velocity just after $t_2$ to judge statements 2 and 3.
walkthrough: Identify the motion: at $t_1$ velocity is constant and high before the parachute opens, at $t_2$ velocity begins to decrease rapidly just after opening, at $t_3$ velocity is constant and low with the parachute open.

Use the velocity-time gradient rule: acceleration $a$ equals the gradient. At $t_1$ and $t_3$ the gradient is zero so $a = 0$. At $t_2$ the downward slope is steepest, so the magnitude of deceleration is largest there. Hence statement 1 is true.

Use vertical force balance: take downwards as positive, then $W - D = ma$. At terminal velocity $a = 0$, so $D = W$. Weight $W$ is unchanged, so drag at $t_1$ equals drag at $t_3$ and both equal weight. Hence statement 2 is true.

Consider drag just after opening: speed is still almost the high $t_1$ value but parachute area is now very large, so $D$ jumps to a value much greater than $W$ to cause the large upward resultant and deceleration. Drag then falls as velocity falls. So drag is not maximum at $t_1$. Hence statement 3 is false.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct and 3 is incorrect. This is option A.
